Description:
The Audi, in conventional mode, transitioned from Byron to San Antonio E/B and waited in the merge pocket for traffic to clear. After approximately 20 seconds of waiting stationary for traffic to clear, a Honda was observed to the left coming over the elevated center island. The Honda hit the right front of Audi and continued to go over another center island at 25-30 mph. Honda came to a stop approximately 75-100 yards from impact heading W/B in the E/B lane. Audi vehicle damage includes right fender, front bumper/fascia.

As reported in the attached Traffic Collision Report, 14-5925, the driver of the Honda was determined to have caused the accident by making an unsafe turning movement in violation of CVC 22107 and was served with a notice of priority reexamination of his driver's license. Attachment: Traffic Collision Report 14-5925

Address: El Camino Real and View St.

Just before the collisions, the driver of the Lexus AV disengaged Autonomous Mode and took maual control of the vehicle in response to the application of the brakes by the Lexus AV's autonomous technology.

A Google Lexus model autonomous vehicle ("google AV") was traveling southbound on Shoreline Blvd. in Mountain View in autonomous mode and was stopped behind traffic at a red light at the intersection of California St. and Rengstorff Ave. A vehicle approaching from behind collided with the rear bumper of the Google AV. Description:
A Google Lexus model autonomous vehicle ("Google AV") was traveling northbound on Grant Rd. in Mountain View approaching the
intersection of Phyllis Ave. and Martens Ave. in autonomous mode. The two vehicles in front of the Google AV, the Google AV, and the
vehicle behind the Google AV were all traveling at a steady speed of - 15 mph. While approaching a green light intersection with stopped traffic on the other side of the intersection, the first vehicle decelerated and came to a stop, keeping clear of the intersection. The vehicle directly in front of the Google AV and the Google AV also decelerated and came to a stop with adequate and similar stopping distances. About 1 second later, the vehicle approaching from the rear struck the Google AV at ~ 17mph and did not appear to decelerate prior to the collision. At the time of the incident, the driver, co-driver, and rear passenger of the Google AV reported some whiplash. They were driven by other team members to a local hospital, where they were evaluated by medical staff and cleared to return to work. The driver of the other vehicle reported minor neck and back pain. The Google AV sustained minor damage to its rear bumper. The other vehicle sustained
significant damage to its front end.

Injuries: The Google AV test driver reported minor back pain and was takento a local hospital by Google employees, where he was evaluated and released by medical staff
Description:
A Google Lexus autonomous vehicle ("Google AV") operating in autonomous mode and traveling northbound on Shoreline BIvd. in
Mountain View in lane two (the second of three lanes) was involved in an accident. As the Google AV approached the intersection of
Shoreline Blvd. and High School way, a pedestrian began to cross the northbound lanes of Shoreline Blvd. in the crosswalk traveling
westbound. The Google AV slowed to yield as it approached the crosswalk, and out of an abundance of caution the Google AV test driver
disengaged the autonomous technology and took control of the vehicle. A vehicle in lane three to the immediate right of, and traveling in the
same direction as, the Google AV was already stopped and yielding the right of way to the pedestrian. A vehicle in the process of changing
lanes from lane one into lane two and approaching from the rear struck the Google AV. The Google AV was travelling 5 mph at the time of
impact, and braking to stop for the crosswalk. The other vehicle was travelling approximately 10 mph at the time of impact.
The Google AV test driver reported minor back pain and was taken to a local hospital by Google employees, where he was evaluated and
released by medical staff. The Google AV co-test driver did not report any injuries. The Google AV sustained minor damage to its rear left
bumper. The other vehicle sustained moderate damage to its front end and was towed from the scene. The driver of the other vehicle did
not report any injuries at the scene.

Address: El Camino Real and Castro St.
Description: A Google Lexus model autonomous vehicle ("google AV") was traveling in autonomous mode eastbound on El Camino Real in Mountain View in the far right-hand lane approaching the Castro St. intersection. Approximately three seconds later, as the Google AV was reentering the center of the lane it made contact with the side of the bus. The google AV was operating in autonomous mode and traveling at less than 2 mph, and the bus was traveling at about 15 mph at the time of contact. The Google AV sustained body damage left front fender, the left front wheel and one of its driver's side sensors. There were no injuries reported at the scene.

Description: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV") was involved in a accident in San Francisco while traveling eastbound on Golden Gate Avenue between Webster and Buchanan streets. The Cruise AV was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the accident. The intersection at Buchanan does not alow for vehicular cross traffic but is controlled by a crosswalk with yellow lights that flash when activated. As the Cruise AV was approaching the crosswalk at Buchanan, the yellow lights were flashing. The Cruise AV slowed, paused briefly before the crosswalk, and then began to proceed. The vehicle immediately behind the CruiseAV, a Toyota Highlander, also slowed and paused in conert with the Cruise AV. A third wehicle, a subaru, located behind the Toyota, did not slow and collided with the Toyota, causing the Subaru's airbags to deploy. That collision pushed the Toyota into the back of the Cruise AV. None of the occupants of the Cruise AV or Toyota reported injuries at the scene, and the driver of the Subaru intended to seek medical evaluation for knee pain from the collision. The Cruise vehicle sustained minimal damage to its rear bumper. The Toyota sustained minor visible damage to its front and rear bumpers. The Subaru sustained minor visible damage to its front end.

A WAYMO LEXUS-MODEL AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE ("WAYMO AV") MADE CONTACT WITH A CURB WHILE IN MANUAL MODE ON MIDDLEFIELD ROAD AT OREGON EXPRESSWAY IN PALO ALTO, CA. THE WAYMO AV WAS TRAVELING EASTBOUND IN AUTONOMOUS MODE IN THE RIGHTMOST LANE OF MIDDLEFIELD ROAD. AS THE VEHICLE CROSSED OREGON EXPRESSWAY, THE WAYMO AV AUTONOMOUS SYSTEM DETECTED THE VEHICLE IN THE LEFT ADJACENT LANE BEGIN TO DRIFT TO THE RIGHT, TOWARD THE WAYMO AV. THE WAYMO AV NUDGED TO THE RIGHTMOST SIDE OF ITS LANE. AS THE LEFT ADJACENT VEHICLE CONTINUED TO DRIFT TOWARDS THE WAYMO AV, THE WAYMO AV TEST DRIVER TOOK MANUAL CONTROL. THE WAYMO AV'S FRONT PASSENGER-SIDE TIRE THEN MADE CONTACT WITH THE RIGHT CURB, CAUSING IT TO DEFLATE. THE OTHER VEHICLE THEN STRAIGHTENED ITS TRAJECTORY IN ITS LANE AND CONTINUED ON. THERE WERE NO INJURIES REPORTED.

Description: A Waymo autonomous vehicle ("Waymo AV") in manual traveling eastbound in the left lane on Almo Street in Palo Alto was involved in a minor collision. A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in conventional mode, was involved in an incident while traveling eastbound on Harrison Street between 12th and 11th Streets. The Cruise A V's driver observed a cyclist traveling in the wrong direction toward the Cruise AV. The cyclist was waving his hands and swerving severely; he appeared to be intoxicated. The driver brought the Cruise AV to a complete stop. The cyclist continued weaving toward the Cruise AV, collided with the Cruise A V's front-right bumper, and fell over. After getting to his feet, the cyclist picked up his bike and deliberately hit the bike's front tire into the passenger side of the Cruise AV. He then pulled on a sensor on the Cmise A V's rear, passenger-side, causing minor damage. With the cyclist off to the side of the vehicle, the driver of the Cruise AV slowly pulled away from the interaction. Police were not present or called to the scene,

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (Cruise AV) initially operating in autonomous mode, was involved in an incident whiletraveling northbound as Potrero Ave turns into Brannan Stret. The charger was in a left-turn only lane in Cruise AV; but instead of turning left, the charger tried to overtake the Cruise AV and to proceed straight as well. At this point, the driver of the Cruise AV took over manual control. As the Charger tried to overtake the Cruise AV and to proceed straight as well. At this point, the driver of the Cruise AV took over manual control. As the Charger cut off the cruise av, it scraped the Cruise AV's front left sensor. At the time of the collision, the Cruise AV was traveling at 4 mph, while the charger was traveling at approx 12 mph. The charger fled the scene without exchanging info. The driver of the Cruise AV called the police to the incident as a hit-and-run but the police were not dispatched and no report was filed.

On October 23rd, a test vehicle operating in manual driving mode was stopped at a red light in the righthand lane of Lawrence Expressway at the intersection with Kifer Road in Santa Clara. A Lexus RX300 attempted to pass through traffic in the adjacent bike lane, and made contact with the test vehicle’s side mirror. No injuries were reported and law enforcement was not called to the scene. The test vehicle sustained minor damage.

On October 26, 2023 at 7:48 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on 13th Street near Bernice Street. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound on 13th Street in the rightmost lane. As the SUV in the left adjacent lane traveling alongside the Waymo AV initiated a right lane change, the front passenger’s side of the SUV made contact with the front driver’s side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged as the test driver transitioned the Waymo AV to manual mode just before the contact. Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“AV”), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was traveling northbound in an alleyway between 26th Street and Princeton Street. As the AV approached the intersection with another alleyway, a Mitsubishi Outlander traveling westbound on a perpendicular alleyway entered the intersection. In response, the Cruise AV operator disengaged from autonomous into manual mode and braked, but shortly thereafter, the AV made contact with the Mitsubishi Outlander, damaging the AV’s front passenger side bumper fascia. The parties exchanged information and there were no reported injuries.

On November 3, 2023 at 3:44 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (Waymo AV) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on 3rd Street at Stevenson Street. The Waymo AV was stopped in the rightmost non-HOV lane on northbound 3rd Street waiting for the intersection at Stevenson Street to clear during a green light. The passenger car behind the Waymo AV was rear-ended by a pickup truck, causing the front of the passenger car to make contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). All three vehicles sustained damage.

On Monday, November 27th, a Nuro Prius operating in manual mode was exiting a garage to begin the work day. At the same time, a Nuro employee was exiting their personal vehicle in the alley behind the garage. The Nuro Prius made contact with the open door of the employee's personal vehicle. No injuries were reported. The employee's personal vehicle had minor damage to the door.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was stopped at a red traffic light on northbound Capp St at the intersection with 24th St in San Francisco. At that time, an SUV (Vehicle 2), heading southbound on Capp St, failed to stop for the red traffic light and entered the intersection, causing a collision with a passenger car (Vehicle 3) that was traveling eastbound on 24th Street. The SUV spun after making contact with the passenger car and collided with the stopped Zoox vehicle, damaging the front bumper on the driver’s side and driver’s side fender, mirror, and sensors on the Zoox vehicle. The police and EMS personnel were called to the scene. The driver of the SUV left the scene without exchanging information. The passenger car appeared to sustain significant damage to the front end. There were no reported injuries

Address: Manhattan Place at West Adams Boulevard
Description:
On January 8, 2023 at 12:05 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Manhattan Place at West Adams Boulevard.  

The Waymo AV was traveling northbound on Manhattan Place when it came to a stop to yield to an oncoming vehicle in a narrow roadway with parked vehicles on both sides of the street. As the oncoming SUV passed the Waymo AV, the driver’s side rear of the SUV made contact with the driver’s side rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage and the SUV left the scene.

A Ghost ADS-equipped car was driving engaged Northbound on Highway 17. As always, there were two safety drivers in the car. Traffic was moving in all four lanes at or near the speed limit. The Ghost vehicle was in the right-middle lane. Another vehicle (the "lead" car) entered into the Ghost car's lane from the right. While there were numerous vehicles ahead of the Ghost car before that vehicle entered the lane, the lead vehicle blocked the view of the lane before it. Throughout the incident, traffic in the other three lanes continued at a steady pace. When the lead vehicle entered into the lane ahead of the Ghost car, the Ghost car applied the brakes to accommodate the intrusion and then continued to match the speed of the lead car. The lead car suddenly slammed the brakes. The Ghost car followed suit, reducing its speed from 19 mps (42.5 mph) to 4.7 mps (10.5 mph) within the next three seconds. The Ghost car was able to match the rapid speed reduction of the lead car and avoid contact. The driver following the Ghost car was not able to respond as quickly as the Ghost ADS. When the following driver began to apply the brakes, the car was about five meters behind and was traveling at 6.5 mps. At the point of impact, the Ghost vehicle was traveling at 4.78 mps (10.7 mph), matching the lead car. There were no injuries. The vehicles suffered only cosmetic damage, the drivers exchanged information, and the Ghost safety drivers returned to home base in conventional mode.

Address: On Bryant St at the Intersection with 6th St
Description: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in manual mode, was stopped for a red traffic light  on northbound Bryant St at the intersection with 6th St in San Francisco with an SUV (Vehicle 2) traveling directly behind . As the signal turned green the Zoox vehicle remained stopped to avoid blocking the intersection as traffic was still stopped ahead. The SUV proceeded to move into the adjacent left lane, when its front bumper on the passenger's side made contact with the driver's side rear bumper of the Zoox vehicle. The front bumper of the SUV appeared to have sustained minor damage. The driver of the SUV left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

Address: On Florida St near the intersection with Divison St
Description: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in manual mode, was traveling southbound on Florida St near the intersection with Division St in San Francisco. The Zoox vehicle slowed to a stop to allow an oncoming box truck (Vehicle 2), attempting to turn left, to clear when the box truck made contact with the driver's side rear camera housing on the Zoox vehicle. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

Address: Cross Street: Terra Bella and Shoreline
Description: On Friday, January 12th, a Nuro Prius operating autonomously was stopped at a red light at the intersection of Shoreline and Terra Bella Ave. A Mazda approaching the intersection failed to completely stop and rear-ended the Nuro Prius. No injuries were reported. Both vehicles sustained minor damage.

Address: On Stockton St near Union St
Description: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was traveling on southbound Stockton St near Union St in San Francisco. The Zoox vehicle slowed to a gradual stop with brake and hazard lights activated during a simulated pick up-drop off maneuver when it was rear-ended by a minivan (Vehicle 2). The rear bumper of the Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage. There were no reported injuries, and police were not called. Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the driver of the minivan may not have been looking ahead at the roadway prior to and at the time of contact.

Address: On 2nd St left turn to E San Fernando St
Description: At approximately 12:56pm, a WeRide vehicle (car 1) was slowing to a stop (< 3mph) on 2nd street at the intersection of East San Fernando st. to turn left in an effort to yield to crossing pedestrians. At this time a Toyota Prius (car 2) traveling (>10mph) had slammed into car 1's rear - causing damage primarily to car 1. Both parties pulled over to a safe location to exchange information but the driver of car 2 could not provide a valid insurance or registration certificate.

On January 26th, a test vehicle operating with the automated driving system engaged was traveling Eastbound on Interstate 580 in Castro Valley when a nearby semi-trailer truck merging from Interstate 238 generated a draft that projected road debris onto the test vehicle. No injuries were reported and law enforcement was not called to the scene. The test vehicle sustained minor damage.

Address: Intersection of Boyce Ave and Fife Ave
Description: On Wednesday, January 31st at approximately 4:20pm, a Nuro Prius was operating in autonomous mode driving south on Boyce Ave in Palo Alto. As the Prius proceeded straight through the intersection of Boyce Ave. and Fife Ave. a Honda CR-V ran the Fife Ave. stop sign and initiated a left turn. The Honda CR-V rear-ended the Nuro Prius, though the Nuro driver took control of the Prius and nudged right in an attempt to avoid impact. Both vehicles sustained de minimis damage. Law enforcement was not involved and there were no injuries reported or VRUs present.

On January 31, 2024 at 5:15 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Potrero Avenue near 22nd Street.The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Potrero Avenue in the leftmost thru lane, adjacent to a dedicated left turn lane on its left. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection with 22nd Street, it came to a stop behind its lead vehicle. The passenger vehicle behind the Waymo AV then attempted to change lanes into the dedicated left turn lane, and made contact with the rear driver side corner of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

Address: Watt Way and West Exposition Boulevard
Description: On February 5, 2024 at 10:01 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a gate at Watt Way and West Exposition Boulevard.The Waymo AV was traveling south on Watt when it approached an automatic gate as it had started to close. The right side of the Waymo AV made contact with the door of the gate. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On February 15th, a test vehicle operating with the automated driving system engaged was traveling Northbound on Highway 101 in Sunnyvale. The safety driver disengaged just prior to running over a piece of metal in the road. No injuries were reported and law enforcement was not called to the scene. The vehicle sustained minor damage.

On February 18, 2024 at 1:03 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on The Embarcadero at Washington Street.The Waymo AV was stopped in traffic for a red light on The Embarcadero southbound when a passenger car approached from behind and made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver's seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage and the passenger car left the scene.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was traveling southwest on Harrison St and turning right onto 13th Street on a green traffic signal. While executing the turn, the Zoox vehicle braked to achieve a minimal risk condition due to an unexpected system fault, the safety operator disengaged, and then was rear ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) that was also turning directly behind the Zoox vehicle. The rear bumper cover and rear radar unit on the Zoox vehicle sustained damage. The hood, front grille and front bumper cover on the passenger car appeared to have sustained damage. There were no reported injuries and police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy, traveling northeast on Mission St, was stopped in lane for a red traffic light at 9th Street. A SamTrans bus (Vehicle 2), with a front-mounted triple-bike rack extending past the width of the bus on the driver's side, was traveling southeast on 9th Street and attempting a right turn onto Mission St. The protruding edge of the bike rack was encroaching into the Zoox vehicle's travel lane as the bus was executing the right hand turn. As the light turned green the Zoox vehicle inched forward and attempted to steer away from the bus. Just as the safety operator disengaged from autonomy, the protruding edge of the bike rack made contact with the driver's side fender on the Zoox vehicle. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

On March 2, 2024 at 8:14 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a dumpster on Odd Fellows Way, at the rear garage exit of 1155 Market Street. The Waymo AV was making a reversing right turn out of the parking garage onto Odd Fellows Way when the rear left corner of the Waymo AV made contact with a dumpster which was next to the curb in the roadway opposite the garage exit.  At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On March 3, 2024 at 3:12 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a pick-up truck near the 2300 block of Cesar Chavez Street.The Waymo AV was traveling westbound on Cesar Chavez Street towards 26th Street when it approached a pick-up truck which was oriented with its rear partially in the roadway on the north side of Cesar Chavez street. The pick-up truck was stationary but its reverse lights were illuminated. The Waymo AV came to a stop momentarily to yield to the pick-up truck, then began moving again to pass the pick-up truck, which had remained stopped. After the Waymo AV started moving, the pick-up truck began reversing further out of the driveway and the rear of the pick-up truck made contact with the right side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

Address: S Figueroa Street at Vince Boulevard
Description: On March 8, 2024 at 12:06 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car near the 1600 block of S. Figueroa Street. The Waymo AV made a left turn from W. 17th Street onto S. Figueroa Street and came to a stop in a queue of stopped traffic. A passenger car traveling straight on S. Figueroa Street behind the Waymo AV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV.  At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage and the passenger car left the scene.

Address: Intersection of Thompson Ave. and Alvin Street
Description: On Tuesday, March 12th, a Nuro Prius vehicle operating in manual was turning left from Alvin Street onto Thompson Ave in Mountain View, California. The Prius vehicle bumped the medium and knocked over a white pylon. The vehicle had minor damage and no injuries were reported. No other vehicles or VRUs were involved. Law enforcement was not involved.

On March 14, 2024 at 2:42 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on S Figueroa Street at 7th Street. The Waymo AV was traveling northeast on S Figueroa Street in the lane adjacent to the rightmost, bus-only lane. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection with 7th Street, it came to a stop behind another vehicle stopped in traffic. As a passenger car was passing the Waymo AV in the bus lane to the right of the Waymo AV, the passenger car made contact with the passenger side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage and the passenger car left the scene.Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 2 of Standing General Order 2021-01.

Address: On 3rd Avenue at S Norfolk St
Description: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in manual mode, was traveling northeast on 3rd Avenue toward Norfolk St in San Mateo. The Zoox vehicle was stopped in the right through lane behind traffic for a red traffic signal, when it was rear ended by a passenger car (Vehicle 2) that was traveling directly behind. There was no visible damage to either vehicle and the police were not called. The safety operator of the Zoox vehicle reported back pain a few days after the collision. Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the driver of the passenger car may not have been looking ahead at the roadway prior to and at the time of contact.

On March 19, 2024 at 7:18 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Division Street at 9th Street. The Waymo AV was traveling west on Division Street after having stopped at the stop sign at Vermont Street and was approaching the intersection with 9th Street when a passenger car approached from behind the Waymo AV, ran the stop sign at Vermont Street, and made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. The front of the passenger car made continuous contact with the rear of the Waymo AV while both vehicles were still in motion for a short period of time before the passenger car slowed down and separated from the AV. The Waymo AV proceeded through the intersection with 9th Street and came to a stop on Division Street west of the intersection with 9th Street. The passenger car then accelerated and the front right corner of the passenger car made contact with the rear left corner of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On March 22, 2024 at 10:00 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car near the 200 block of Church Street before Market Street. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Church Street towards the intersection with Market Street when it came to a stop behind an SUV which was stopped in-lane to load passengers. Another SUV approached from behind the Waymo AV and came to a stop. The lead SUV finished loading passengers and proceeded forward to the stop line at Market Street, and the Waymo AV proceeded forward as well. The trailing SUV proceeded forward and the front of the SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV.  At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage and the SUV left the scene.

On March 28, 2024 at 7:30 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Louisiana Avenue at Kerwood Avenue. While making a tight left turn from southbound Kerwood Avenue onto northeastbound Louisiana Avenue, the Waymo AV made contact with the driver side of a parked passenger car. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

On March 30, 2024 at 1:33 AM PT, a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Jerrold Avenue at Barneveld Avenue.The Waymo AV was stopped at a stop sign on Jerrold Avenue and yielding to a pickup truck that was in the intersection making a left turnfrom Barneveld Avenue onto Jerrold Avenue when the front right corner of the SUV, which was traveling behind the Waymo AV, madecontact with the rear left corner of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomousmode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle in autonomy, traveling westbound on 3rd Avenue toward Foster City Blvd in Foster City drove over an in-lane utility valve box with a displaced valve cover. The Zoox vehicle sustained damage to the undercarriage. There were no reported injuries and police were not called.

On April 11, 2024 at 10:14 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Vallejo Street at Stockton Street. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound on Vallejo Street and stopped at a red light. A heavy truck was turning left onto Vallejo Street from Stockton Street. As the heavy truck approached, the Waymo AV started to slowly reverse to make more space. The test driver transitioned to manual, and the driver’s side of the heavy truck and the driver's side front corner of the Waymo AV made contact. The heavy truck left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On April 13, 2024 at 3:35 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a pickup truck on Bayshore Boulevard near Boutwell Street. The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Bayshore Boulevard in the far right lane when it passed a pickup truck that was stopped in the bike lane. As the Waymo passed the pickup truck, the driver of the pickup truck opened the driver’s side door and the door made contact with the Waymo’s passenger side wing mirror and rear right sensor housing.  At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver's seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle, operating in manual mode, was traveling north on Folsom Street, preparing to turn left onto 21st Street in San Francisco when the front wheel on the driver's side rode over a traffic island to the left side of the Zoox vehicle. The sidewall of the tire was damaged as a result of the interaction. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

On April 23, 2024, a Pony.ai autonomous vehicle (AV) scraped a curb on Lakeview Blvd near the intersection of Lakeview Blvd & Gateway Blvd in Fremont, CA. The vehicle was operating in supervised autonomous ("Drivered") mode. There were no other vehicles, pedestrians, or road users involved.Following the incident, the safety operator promptly drove the AV, in manual mode, to Pony.ai's Fremont office. There were no injuriesreported, and the police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was stopped at a red light in the right travel lane on southbound 11th Street at the intersection with Bryant/Division Streets in San Francisco. After the light turned green, the Zoox vehicle entered the intersection and began bearing right onto southbound Bryant Street when a lane-splitting motorcycle (Vehicle 2) operator maneuvered around other traffic and quickly came up on the rear of the Zoox vehicle, traversing laterally in lane from the left to the right side of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle braked and then the Zoox vehicle operator disengaged. The motorcycle then struck the passenger’s side of the rear bumper and quarter panel on the Zoox vehicle and the motorcycle and its operator fell to the ground. The motorcycle operator appeared to have scraped his hands, but declined medical attention. The motorcycle sustained minor damage to the fairing, left side mirror, and front and rear left turn signal lens and the Zoox vehicle did not sustain damage. The motorcycle operator left the scene without exchanging their information. The police were not called.

Address: I-280 Junipero Serra FWY between exits 49B and 51
Description: On May 8, 2024 at 11:16 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a wild animal (raccoon) on Interstate 280 Junipero Serra Freeway between exits 49B and 51. The Waymo AV was traveling eastbound on Interstate 280 in autonomous mode when a raccoon ran into the roadway from the left side of the highway in front of the Waymo AV. The Waymo AV test driver transitioned to manual mode shortly before the front driver’s side of the Waymo AV made contact with the raccoon. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

Address: Interstate 10 East between Exit 2 and Exit 3A
Description: On May 13, 2024 at 12:58 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, CA was in a collision involving a passenger car on eastbound Interstate 10 between Exit 2 and Exit 3A. The Waymo AV was traveling with a test driver present behind a box truck in the number 3 lane of eastbound Interstate 10 near the Bundy Drive overpass when a passenger car traveling at a high rate of speed approached the Waymo AV from behind. The passenger car partially entered the number 2 lane as the front right corner of the passenger car made contact with the rear left corner of the Waymo AV. The passenger car then made contact with the center median and came to a stop. The Waymo AV was transitioned into manual mode, and the test driver stopped the Waymo AV to the right-hand shoulder. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

Address: Auto Mall Pkwy, Auto Mall Pkwy & Grimmer Blvd
Description: On May 15, 2024, the front right bumper of a Pony.ai autonomous vehicle (AV) scraped against a flexible plastic traffic pylon on Auto Mall Pkwy near the intersection of Auto Mall Pkwy & Grimmer Blvd, in Fremont, CA. The vehicle was operating in supervised autonomous (“Drivered”)  mode. There were no other vehicles, pedestrians, or road users involved.Following the incident, the safety operator pulled over in a safe location and confirmed there was only minor cosmetic damage to the front bumper of the AV. The safety operator then promptly drove the vehicle, in manual mode, to Pony.ai’s Fremont office. There were no injuries, and the police were not called.

On May 17, 2024 at 11:45 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Interstate 280 North between exits 54B and 55. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Interstate 280 in the rightmost lane in autonomous mode with a test driver seated in the driver's seated position when it approached a slow-moving heavy truck equipped with a truck-mounted light matrix displaying a yellow arrow indicating that traffic should merge to the left. The Waymo AV slowed down behind the heavy truck and the test driver transitioned the Waymo AV to manual mode. The test driver stopped the Waymo AV and activated the left turn signal. Several vehicles passed the Waymo AV on the left side before the test driver manually initiated a left lane change, and the front passenger side of a passenger car which was passing the Waymo AV on the left made contact with the front driver side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode.  Both vehicles sustained damage.

On May 20, 2024 at 3:02 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on 14th Street at Folsom Street. The Waymo AV was traveling east on 14th Street and came to a stop at a red light at the intersection with Folsom Street to prepare for a left turn. When the light turned green, the Waymo AV proceeded into the intersection. As it did so, a passenger car traveling southbound on Folsom Street at a high rate of speed entered the intersection against a red traffic light. The front of the passenger car made contact with the driver’s side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage, and the passengers of the passenger car left the scene on foot.

On Wednesday, May 22, 2024 at approximately 3:45pm PST, a Nuro Prius operating in manual mode bumped a pedestrian at the
intersection of Webster Street and Middlefield Road in Palo Alto, California.

The Nuro Prius was in autonomous mode when it approached the intersection and came to a stop at the stop bar on Webster Street. It is
a two-way stop with the traffic on Middlefield having right of way. The Nuro Prius nudged forward due to an occlusion.The Nuro operator judged the nudging to be too far and disengaged autonomous mode to reverse in manual. When reversing, the operator bumped a pedestrian crossing the street behind the Nuro Prius. 

The pedestrian was not injured and after speaking with the operator, left the scene without providing additional information. There was no damage to the vehicle and law enforcement was not involved.

Address: Chess Drive approaching Foster City Blvd
Description: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was traveling westbound on Chess Drive in Foster City when a parallel-parked passenger car (Vehicle 2) abruptly entered the Zoox vehicle’s travel lane from a parking space in the right parking lane without yielding or activating a turn signal. Vehicle 2 made contact with the right front side and wheel of the Zoox vehicle, and the Zoox vehicle made contact with the driver side door and left front tire/wheel well of the passenger car. Both vehicles sustained moderate damage and the Zoox vehicle was towed from the scene. There were no injuries and police were not called.

On June 3, 2024 at 4:54 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Marina Del Rey, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Admiralty Way at Bali Way. The Waymo AV was making a left turn from the rightmost dedicated left turn lane on Admiralty Way into lane two of three lanes in the eastbound direction of Bali Way. A passenger car was also making a left turn from the leftmost dedicated left turn lane (leftmost lane). The passenger car had made the turn onto Bali Way and was partially in the number 1 lane (leftmost) and partially in the number 2 lane (middle) when the front passenger side of the passenger car made contact with the rear driver side of the Waymo AV, which was traveling in the number 2 lane (middle). At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

On June 4, 2024 at 6:26 PM PT  a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Lombard Street at Fillmore Street. The Waymo AV was stopped in traffic for a red light on eastbound Lombard Street when an SUV traveling at a high rate of speed changed lanes and approached the Waymo AV from behind. The front of the SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On June 5, 2024 at 1:12 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on 29th Avenue near Lawton Street.The Waymo AV was parked at the curb on the right side of 29th Avenue when a passenger car in front of the Waymo AV began to reverse to parallel park. The passenger car’s rear driver side corner made contact with the front driver side corner of the parked Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

Address: E San Carlos St & S 4th St
Description: At approximately 10:33am, a WeRide vehicle (car 1) was stopped at a red traffic light on E San Carlos st. about to turn right on S 4th St. At this time a Toyota RAV4 (car 2) approached from behind traveling at a speed of (>10mph) and slammed into car 1's rear - causing damages to car 1. Car 1 sustained damages on rear bumper and rear sensors. Both parties pulled over to a safe location to exchange information. Car 2's driver didn't have an up-to-date registration card for the vehicle.

On June 11, 2024 at 12:07 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Santa Monica, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Maple Street near 10th Street. The Waymo AV was maneuvering out of a curbside parallel parking space at the curb on the south side of Maple Street when the passenger side front corner of the Waymo AV made contact with the driver side back corner of an SUV parked in front of the AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

At 3:51pm, a WeRide vehicle (Car1) was attempting to make a u-turn at 6 mph on Northwestern parkway. During the u-turn maneuver, a white chevy cruze (Car 2) traveling at 23 mph, having just made a right turn off of Walsh Ave., approached from behind on northwestern parkway. Car 2 steered left just before the impact but still clipped the front left side bumper of Car 1 with its (car2's) right side.
